steps.text: Speed tells us how fast something moves. It's simply distance divided by time. Let's calculate it.
Enter a distance and a time, then tap “Calculate”.
Speed = distance ÷ time. So 100 metres in 20 seconds is 100 ÷ 20 = 5 metres per second.
Keep the units matched — metres with seconds gives m/s; kilometres with hours gives km/h. That's the whole idea of speed.

coach.mission: Calculate speed from a distance and a time.
whenStuck: Divide the distance by the time to get the speed.
whenWrong: Speed = distance ÷ time — divide, don't multiply.
Keep units matched: metres + seconds → m/s; km + hours → km/h.
whenCorrect: Right — distance ÷ time gives the speed.
Good — and the units follow the distance and time you used.
coach.done: You've calculated speed from distance and time. Try more, or move on when you're ready.
